cards.lead: Chlorpromazine and antipsychotic drugs in France
cards.note: The 1952 publication found is Laborit and colleagues' February 1952 report, which concerned surgical patients and noted effects outside surgery. The Delay and Deniker psychiatric trials are described without a date in the source opened, and the 1950 synthesis was not found. Origin is set to unknown because no source opened says the drug was the first of its kind or was reached independently.
cards.name: Chlorpromazine as a psychiatric drug in Paris
cards.summary: Chlorpromazine, first tested in surgery, was then used by Delay and Deniker at Sainte-Anne to treat psychotic patients in 1952.
cards.description: Henri Laborit's team published a report in February 1952 on chlorpromazine, which they had tested on surgical patients and which caused a disinterested state when used in other situations. Jean Delay and Pierre Deniker at the Sainte-Anne hospital in Paris then gave it alone, in successive doses, to psychotic patients and reported that it subdued hallucinations and delusions. Rhône Poulenc marketed it in France in 1952.
cards.origin_note: The source opened describes Rhône Poulenc developing the drug, but does not say whether it was the first such drug or was reached independently.

impact.note: Scores kept from the lead; the source supports the change in treatment but not the claim about hospital populations.

events.label: February 1952
events.statement: Laborit and colleagues published a report on chlorpromazine in February 1952, noting a disinterested state in patients when it was used outside surgery.
events.quote: In the report that he and his colleagues published in February 1952
events.locator: Section: Delay and Deniker: Psychiatric Trials (preceding section on Laborit)

events.statement: Chlorpromazine was first marketed in France in 1952.
events.quote: First marketed in France in 1952, and then in the United States as Thorazine in 1954

sources.title: Paul Charpentier, Henri-Marie Laborit, Simone Courvoisier, Jean Delay, and Pierre Deniker

open_questions: Date of Delay and Deniker's psychiatric trial report; the Wikipedia claim of May 1952 is not sourced here.
Verify the 1950 synthesis at Rhône-Poulenc and the 38-patient figure before using them.
Whether the drug was the first antipsychotic, and whether any earlier antipsychotic use is recorded.

cards.name: Quarantine at Ragusa
cards.summary: The Adriatic port of Ragusa set a 30-day isolation for ships and 40 days for land travellers from plague areas in 1377.
cards.description: In 1377 Ragusa, now Dubrovnik, set up a quarantine against plague. Ships from infected or suspected areas were held for thirty days and land travellers for forty. Earlier observation that epidemic disease travelled by ship had stimulated the idea of quarantine.
cards.origin_note: The review presents the 1377 Ragusa measure as the setting up of a genuine quarantine, and the sources opened show no earlier one.
cards.why: Earlier observations that epidemic diseases were transported by ships stimulated the notion of quarantines.

events.statement: A genuine quarantine was set up at Ragusa in 1377, with thirty days' isolation for ships from infected areas and forty for land travellers.
events.quote: Accordingly, a genuine quarantine was set up in 1377 in the Venetian trading station at Ragusa

sources.title: Quinto Tiberio Angelerio and New Measures for Controlling Plague in 16th-Century Alghero, Sardinia

open_questions: The review calls Ragusa a Venetian trading station, which conflicts with its usual description as an independent republic; settle the political status.
The exact decree date (27 July 1377) and the Latin title come from secondary sources and need the Liber viridis or a scholarly edition.
The lead's Venice lazaretto of 1423 and Venetian health magistracy were not checked.
Whether isolation of lepers before 1377 counts as an earlier quarantine.

cards.note: Lillie's 1998 Nature correspondence disputes the claim that Ensisheim has the earliest unequivocal healed trepanation, citing compelling evidence of earlier surgery in eastern Europe during the Mesolithic. The date of 5100 BCE is Alt and colleagues' claim as quoted by Lillie. The Mesolithic eastern European case was not dated from an opened source, so it is not given as an event.
cards.name: Trepanation at Ensisheim, Alsace
cards.summary: A healed trepanation in a Neolithic burial at Ensisheim, Alsace, dated to about 5100 BCE and once claimed as the earliest unequivocal case.
cards.description: The skull of a man of about 50 from a burial at Ensisheim in Alsace had two trepanations, one fully healed and one partly healed, showing that the patient survived. Alt and colleagues dated the find to 5100 BCE and called it the earliest unequivocal evidence for trepanation. Lillie argued in 1998 that earlier surgery of this kind was carried out in eastern Europe during the Mesolithic.
cards.origin_note: The sources opened do not address whether the Ensisheim operation was independent of other places.

events.label: c. 5100 BCE
events.statement: Healed trepanations in a skull from Ensisheim, Alsace, were dated by Alt and colleagues to 5100 BCE, a date that Lillie reports without endorsing as the earliest.
events.quote: from Ensisheim, Alsace, dated to 5100 bc

sources.title: Cranial surgery dates back to Mesolithic

open_questions: Date and location of the Mesolithic eastern European trepanation (Vasilyevka II, per Archaeology magazine 1998, not opened); the date is not established here.
Read Alt et al., Nature 387, 360 (1997), for the original dating method and the 5100 BCE date.
Motive for the operation, which the Archaeology magazine report says is unknown.

cards.note: The earliest dated trepanations in the 2018 study are about 400 BCE on Peru's southern coast, as the lead said. The independence claim is not supported by any source opened, so origin is set to unknown.
cards.name: Trepanation on Peru's south coast and in the Andes
cards.summary: Peruvian surgeons trepanned skulls from about 400 BCE, with survival rising from about 40 percent at Paracas to over 70 percent under the Inca.
cards.description: A study of about 800 Peruvian skulls found that the earliest trepanations, from the Paracas region of the south coast, date to about 400 BCE. Survival was about 40 percent in the Paracas period, and Verano reports Inca rates over 70 percent, inferred from healing in the bone. The sources give no evidence for independence from other places.
cards.origin_note: The sources opened do not say whether Andean trepanation was reached independently, so the lead's independence claim is not evidenced.

events.label: 400 BCE
events.statement: The earliest skulls in the 2018 study showing trepanation date back to about 400 BCE and come from Peru's southern coast.
events.quote: dated back to 400 B.C. , and came from Peru’s southern coast

sources.title: Amazing Things We’ve Learned From 800 Ancient Skull Surgeries

open_questions: The 2018 study itself (Kushner and Verano, Science) was not opened; check its survival figures.
Whether any Andean trepanation is independent of other places.
The Peruvian Times claim of 3000 BCE is unsupported and was not used.

cards.note: The Japanese Society of Anesthesiologists dates the first operation to 13 October 1804, as the lead said. Its account states that Hanaoka knew of Hua Tuo's Chinese anaesthetic, so the origin is derived, not independent. The lead's Hirayama and Kii Province were not in the source opened, so the place is given as Japan.
cards.name: Herbal general anaesthesia in Japan
cards.summary: Seishu Hanaoka removed a breast tumour under a herbal general anaesthetic on 13 October 1804, drawing on Chinese knowledge.
cards.description: Seishu Hanaoka used a herbal mixture of datura and aconite, which he called mafutsusan, to remove a breast cancer tumour from an unconscious patient on 13 October 1804. He knew of the third-century Chinese anaesthetic Mafeisan used by Hua Tuo, so the method was derived from an earlier achievement. The Japanese Society of Anesthesiologists records this as the first such surgery known.
cards.origin_note: The Japanese Society of Anesthesiologists says Hanaoka knew of Hua Tuo's Mafeisan from the third century in China, which is evidenced transmission of knowledge.

events.label: 13 October 1804
events.statement: Hanaoka removed a breast cancer tumour under general anaesthesia on 13 October 1804, the first such operation known.
events.quote: removed a breast cancer tumor for the first time in the world on October 13, 1804

open_questions: Primary documentation of the 1804 operation, which the sources opened do not give.
The formula and its sources in Chinese and Dutch medicine.
Spread of the method through Hanaoka's school and why it was not carried on.
The birth and death years vary between sources, so none are given.

cards.note: The Kuahuqiao lacquer is dated to about 8000 years ago, which is about 6050 BCE, not 6000 to 5000 BCE as the lead said. The Heritage Science article that was opened gives this date and cites Kuahuqiao as the earliest lacquerware. The Jomon claim at Kakinoshima was not opened.
cards.name: Lacquer coating at Kuahuqiao, China
cards.summary: Lacquer on objects at Kuahuqiao in Zhejiang, dated to about 8000 years ago, is among the earliest known in East Asia.
cards.description: Lacquer from the sap of the lacquer tree was used as a coating and adhesive on objects at the Kuahuqiao site in Zhejiang, China. The Heritage Science article says the earliest lacquerware was found there, about 8000 years ago or earlier. Its origin in relation to Japanese lacquer is not settled by the sources opened.
cards.origin_note: The sources opened do not say whether Chinese and Japanese lacquer are independent or which is earlier.

events.label: c. 6050 BCE
events.statement: Lacquerware at the Kuahuqiao site in Zhejiang is dated to about 8000 years ago, roughly 6050 BCE by subtracting from 1950.
events.quote: The earliest lacquerware dating back to about 8000 years ago or even earlier was found at Kuahuqiao site

sources.title: pH-dependent warping behaviors of ancient lacquer films excavated in Shanxi, China

open_questions: Wu et al. (2018, Journal of Archaeological Science) on the Kuahuqiao bow was not opened; check the ELISA identification.
The Kakinoshima (Jomon, Hokkaido) lacquer claimed at about 7000 BCE needs its own record and a comparison of dates.
Whether Chinese and Japanese lacquer are independent, and which is first.
The Hemudu bowl dates (6000 to 7000 years ago) are from secondary sources and were not checked.
